title: QBR: Nereid - Stability, Spend & Roadmap Sprint Kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share 90-day cost breakdown and token-level bucket CSV
Liam to run a 48hr stress benchmark with dedicated capacity and quieter quantized variant by 2027-03-16
Sofia to schedule follow-up deep-dive on rollout policy integration (canary + fallback) week of 3/21
Customer to confirm compliance contacts for SOC2 and data residency by 2027-03-12
action_items: Liam Chen: run 48hr stress benchmark (dedicated + quantized) - due 2027-03-16
Maya Patel: share tokenized cost CSV and perf profile for their top-5 endpoints - due 2027-03-11
Sofia Alvarez: set up follow-up call for rollout/A/B tests - due 2027-03-18
Olivia Grant: provide list of PII/data classes and retention window - due 2027-03-12
meeting_header: Date: 2027-03-09 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Sofia (Redwood); Olivia, Rajat, Tanya, Marco, Samira (Nereid)
summary: Quarterly review focused on stability incidents last quarter, cost drivers from conversational routing, proposal for a sprint to tighten rollout and cost controls, and agreement to run benchmarks and share detailed cost/usage artifacts.
topics: Incident recap: two latency spikes during friday peak
Token-level cost drivers and embedding re-runs
Dedicated vs hosted for 3 mission-critical routes
VPC/private deployment checklist and compliance questions
Roadmap: canary rollouts, automatic fallback, cost guardrails
transcript: 00:00:05 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, and we'll get into the QBR. I think we have 55 minutes.
00:00:12 Olivia Grant: Hi Maya, Olivia here. Rajat, Marco, Tanya and Samira from Nereid. Thanks for organizing.
00:00:18 Rajat Singh: Hey all. I might be lower audio, apologies in advance.

00:00:25 Maya Patel: No worries. Goal for today: run through the incidents, cost picture, backlog items and agree on a sprint plan for stability and spend optimization. Liam, can you start with the latency incident recap?

00:00:38 Liam Chen: Sure. So quick summary — on Feb 22 we saw two notable spikes in 95th and occasional 99th percentiles, both during the 09:00 to 10:30 PST window. Root cause was a combination of an unbounded request pattern from a partner connector and a bad quantization fallback that increased decoding time, plus a small KV cache eviction storm. We mitigated by temporarily throttling that partner and enabling a fallback to a lower context model.

00:01:05 Marco DeLuca: Right, and to add — our side saw the spike manifest as a queue buildup on the dedicated pool, which then bled into hosted routes because we had routing thresholds at 80% and no graceful degradation. We want smarter routing not to fail the rest of the platform.

00:01:20 Liam Chen: Yeah, that is where Redwood's smart routing could help, with region and capacity policies plus automatic fallback to compatible variants. We also recommended prefix caching for the common prompt fragments which reduced token work in tests.
00:01:34 Rajat Singh: Quick Q — you mentioned 'compatible variants'— is that quantized 8-bit models or smaller sequence-length tuned variants? Cost delta?

00:01:42 Liam Chen: Both. Usually we serve a larger FP16 for quality critical flows, and have quantized 8-bit variants for scale. For Nereid's highest-volume route, estimates show about 35–45% token-cost reduction with 8-bit plus minimal latency impact in our synth benchmark. But quality regressions need evals — we can attach a small eval set.

00:02:05 Tanya Brooks: From finance perspective, that 40% is attractive, but we need hard numbers. Also curious about how autoscaling and reserved capacity interplay— if we go Dedicated, what's the minimum commit and can we burst to hosted?

00:02:18 Maya Patel: Good question. Dedicated is typically a reserved pool; you can set burst policies to spill to hosted but that's a pricing tradeoff. We'll share a cost model CSV that breaks down per-token and per-embedding unit across FP16 vs 8-bit and across dedicated vs hosted. That should give you the monthly projection under your traffic profile.
00:02:33 Olivia Grant: Perfect. Also security: Marco flagged we need clarity on KMS integration and audit logs. We're regulated so SSO, event logs and retention need to be explicit.

00:02:42 Sofia Alvarez: We'll include our SOC2 and encryption whitepaper. For private deployments, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit log forwarding; we can sketch the architecture and the onboarding checklist.
00:02:55 Samira Khan: Can you confirm data residency? We have EU-only customer subsets. Can routing honor data residency constraints?

00:03:02 Liam Chen: Yes, routing policies support region pins and can enforce run-in-region only. For on-prem or VPC we can keep inference in your environment. There are some differences in observability surface area — we can walk through those.
00:03:14 Marco DeLuca: Observability — the token-level traces we have now are pretty coarse. We need per-route latency breakdown and payload sizes to debug the KV cache eviction. Is that exposed?

00:03:22 Liam Chen: We emit per-request traces and per-token cost breakdown. I suspect the eviction storm was correlated to a pattern of long prefix hits and then a sudden shift to new prompts causing the cache to thrash. We'll pull the traces and annotate them for you.
00:03:36 Olivia Grant: On the evals you mentioned — we need to include our safety checks and hallucination metrics. If quantized model bumps hallucination rate by X% we can't accept it.

00:03:45 Liam Chen: Totally. We'll run head-to-head on your evals and include safety filters; if there's a regression we can route that route to FP16 and keep the rest on 8-bit while we tune prompts or distillation.
00:03:55 Tanya Brooks: Regarding costs, one more Q — do you provide daily usage burn reports and anomaly alerts? We wanted an alert when spend deviates more than 20% from forecast.
00:04:03 Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we have quota alerts and we can set an economics alert on token burn that triggers email and Slack. We can also push a CSV daily to your finance S3.

00:04:12 Rajat Singh: For the sprint plan, we want to prioritize (1) eliminating the KV eviction storm, (2) cost pilot on high-volume route with 8-bit, (3) tighter routing policies. Timeline 2 weeks for initial benchmarks, 4–6 weeks for rollout. Thoughts?

00:04:24 Maya Patel: Sounds good. Proposed immediate deliverables: Liam runs the benchmark, Maya shares cost breakdown, Sofia schedules the follow-ups. Then a canary plan for rollout into production with rollback criteria.
00:04:33 Olivia Grant: For rollback criteria — we need a clear guardrail set: latency > 250ms p95 or hallucination rate +2% triggers rollback. We need those captured in the runbook.

00:04:41 Liam Chen: We'll draft the runbook. Quick note — the latency numbers are dependent on sequence length; your average request length is 120 tokens but p95 goes to 600 for some analytics queries. We should set SLOs by route class.

00:04:55 Marco DeLuca: Could you also confirm the behavior when a dedicated pool hits saturation? We want automatic fallback to hosted but only if encrypted payloads are allowed to leave the VPC — otherwise it should reject.

00:05:05 Maya Patel: Good point. Fallback policy can be conditional. If payload contains PII flagged by your prefilter, we can block fallback and surface a rate limit instead. That is configurable in the routing policy.
00:05:15 Rajat Singh: Any suggested immediate config changes to avoid repeat spikes?

00:05:19 Liam Chen: Short term: set lower concurrency cap per partner connector, enable prefix cache for heavy prompts, and add a token cap on single requests. Medium term: dedicate a small reserve for peak windows and run a chaos test to validate routing.

00:05:31 Tanya Brooks: From finance I want a scenario analysis: if we move 3 top routes to 8-bit with canary 10% traffic, what's expected monthly savings and worst-case cost if we spill to hosted during peaks?

00:05:41 Maya Patel: We'll create three scenarios in the CSV: conservative (10% quantized), aggressive (50%), and mixed with burst-to-hosted toggled. That will have assumptions about token distribution and average context window.
00:05:52 Samira Khan: On product roadmap alignment — we plan to add multi-step retrieval augmentation soon. How does that change cost profile?

00:05:58 Liam Chen: Retrieval adds embedding and for each step possibly an extra generation. That multiplies token work; recommend caching embedding vectors and using lightweight rerankers where possible. We'll help estimate per-user costs for multi-step flows.
00:06:10 Olivia Grant: Can you also include recommended prompt engineering changes? Some of our prompts are verbose and could trim 20–30 tokens safely.
00:06:15 Liam Chen: Yes, prompt compression is low hanging fruit. We can run a pilot with 5 canonical prompts and measure quality delta.

00:06:22 Maya Patel: Ok moving toward wrap: let's confirm commitments and owners. Liam: run the 48hr benchmark and annotate traces. Maya: cost CSV and scenario analysis. Sofia: schedule two follow-ups — one for the rollout runbook and one for SOC2/KMS review. Olivia: provide eval set and PII categories.
00:06:36 Olivia Grant: Will do. Expect the eval set by Friday.
00:06:40 Marco DeLuca: One small ask — can we get a short playbook on how Redwood handles KV cache warmup across restarts? We saw cold cache penalties.
00:06:47 Liam Chen: We'll include cache warmup recommendations and an approach to prime the cache during off-peak with synthetic prefixes.
00:06:55 Tanya Brooks: Anything else on compliance?
00:06:58 Sofia Alvarez: We'll send the SOC2 and encryption docs and a short checklist for Private/VPC onboarding. We'll also list time estimates for each security review item.
00:07:07 Rajat Singh: For the dedicated commit question — what's the minimum expected?

00:07:10 Maya Patel: Typically the entry point for dedicated is a 3-month trial pool with a modest commit. We'll outline options: 3-month trial, 6-month reserve, or 12-month committed capacity with discounts. We'll include burst behaviour for each.
00:07:22 Samira Khan: Ok, sounds like a plan. Any blockers to start the sprint?
00:07:26 Olivia Grant: No blockers, just waiting on the cost CSV and the benchmark schedule.
00:07:30 Maya Patel: Great. We'll target the benchmark to start Monday 2027-03-13 and report mid-week. Any final notes?
00:07:38 Tanya Brooks: Please cc finance on the cost exports.
00:07:41 Sofia Alvarez: Will do. I'll include the finance alias.
00:07:45 Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the two deep dives. Chat for anything else. Meeting adjourned.
00:07:53 Speaker 7: thanks all bye
00:08:02 [end of recording]
